# Testing Authentication

```python
from flaxon import Flaxon
from flaxon.testing import TestClient
from flaxon.security import JWTBackend


def test_authentication():

    app = Flaxon("test-app")

    backend = JWTBackend(
        secret_key="test-secret"
    )


    @app.post("/login")
    async def login(request):

        data = await request.json()

        token = await backend.create_token({
            "username": data["username"]
        })


        return {
            "token": token
        }



    client = TestClient(app)


    response = client.post(
        "/login",
        json_data={
            "username": "alice"
        }
    )


    token = response.json()["token"]


    response = client.get(
        "/protected",
        headers={
            "Authorization": f"Bearer {token}"
        }
    )
```

# Complete Test Example

```python
import pytest

from flaxon import Flaxon, HTTPException
from flaxon.testing import TestClient


app = Flaxon("test-app")

users = []


@app.get("/")
async def home():

    return {
        "message": "Welcome"
    }


@app.get("/users")
async def list_users():

    return users



@app.post("/users")
async def create_user(request):

    data = await request.json()

    user = {
        "id": len(users) + 1,
        **data
    }

    users.append(user)

    return {
        "created": True,
        "user": user
    }



@app.get("/users/<int:user_id>")
async def get_user(user_id):

    for user in users:

        if user["id"] == user_id:

            return user


    raise HTTPException(
        404,
        "User not found"
    )



@pytest.fixture
def client():

    return TestClient(app)



def test_home(client):

    response = client.get("/")

    assert response.status_code == 200

    assert response.json()["message"] == "Welcome"



def test_create_user(client):

    response = client.post(
        "/users",
        json_data={
            "name": "Alice"
        }
    )


    assert response.status_code == 200

    assert response.json()["created"] is True
```

* Test background tasks.

# Source: docs/guides/admin-resources.md

# Declarative admin resources

A `Resource` turns a model into a full admin without hand-writing views. It is
**additive**: `admin.register(Model, list_display=[...], ...)` keeps working
exactly as before, and every option below maps onto the existing registry.

## A model becomes an admin in under ten lines

```python
from flaxon.admin.resources import Resource, Text, Email

class CustomerResource(Resource):
    model = Customer
    fields = [Text("name", required=True).searchable(), Email("email")]

dashboard.register(CustomerResource)
```

`dashboard.register(CustomerResource)` derives `fields`, `list_display`,
`search_fields`, `list_filter`, `readonly_fields` and the admin URL name from
the declaration. The generated routes are the same ones the legacy registry
uses: `/admin/customer`, `/admin/customer/add`, `/admin/customer/<id>/edit`.

## Fields, options and server-side rules

Every field validates on the server with the same `flaxon.validation` field the
JSON API uses. Declarations stay readable because options are fluent:

```python
from flaxon.admin.resources import Resource, Number, Select, Text

class OrderResource(Resource):
    model = Order
    fields = [
        Text("reference", required=True, min_length=3).searchable().sortable(),
        Select("status", choices=[("new", "New"), ("paid", "Paid")]).filterable(),
        Number("total", minimum=0).help("Order value").show_on_index(),
        Text("internal_note").readonly().show_on_form(False),
    ]

cleaned, errors = OrderResource().validate(
    {"reference": "ORD-1", "status": "new", "total": "42"}
)
assert errors == {}
assert cleaned["total"] == 42
```

Available fluent options: `sortable()`, `searchable()`, `filterable()`,
`readonly()`, `rules(*validators)`, `help(text)`, `show_on_index()`,
`show_on_detail()`, `show_on_form()`, and `depends_on(field, value)`.
`depends_on` hides and disables a control until another field has the required
value; the server still validates every submitted field.

## Field catalogue

| Group | Fields |
|---|---|
| Text | `Text`, `Textarea`, `Slug`, `Password`, `Code`, `Markdown` (sanitized) |
| Numbers and choices | `Number`, `Currency`, `Boolean`, `Select`, `Badge`, `Color` |
| Dates and media | `Date`, `DateTime`, `Image`, `File` |
| Structured | `JSON`, `KeyValue`, `Tags` |
| Relations | `BelongsTo` (async searchable select), `HasMany` (related table + create), `ManyToMany` (attach/detach with `pivot_fields`) |

Output is HTML-escaped by default. `Markdown` additionally sanitizes HTML and
strips dangerous URL schemes using Flaxon's existing `Sanitizer`.

## Relations and the N+1 guard

Index columns that follow relations are loaded eagerly, so a page of records
does not issue one query per row:

```python
from flaxon.admin.resources import Resource, BelongsTo, HasMany, Text

class OrderResource(Resource):
    model = Order
    fields = [
        Text("reference").show_on_index(),
        BelongsTo("customer").show_on_index(),
        HasMany("lines").show_on_index(),
    ]

assert OrderResource().select_related_names() == ["customer"]
assert OrderResource().prefetch_related_names() == ["lines"]
```

`BelongsTo` columns use `select_related`; `HasMany` and `ManyToMany` columns use
`prefetch_related`. A query-count regression test asserts the statement count
stays bounded as the number of rows grows.

## Validation failures

A failed form re-renders with per-field messages and writes nothing:

```python
from flaxon.admin.resources import Resource, Email, Text

class SignupResource(Resource):
    model = Customer
    fields = [Text("name", required=True), Email("email")]

cleaned, errors = SignupResource().validate({"name": "A", "email": "bad"})
assert "email" in errors
```


---

# Source: docs/guides/admin-metrics.md

# Metrics and dashboard cards

Flaxon Admin can render SQL-backed metric cards on the dashboard index and on
each model's change list. The five metric kinds are `Value`, `Trend`,
`Partition`, `Progress` and `Table`.

Metrics are **additive**: registration never changes the legacy
`register(Model, **options)` path. Every calculation runs as a SQL aggregate
through Tortoise (`count`, `annotate`/`group_by`), not a Python row loop. Charts
are inline SVG — no JavaScript, no CDN, theme-aware through `currentColor`, and
carrying a `<title>`/`<desc>` text alternative for assistive technology.

## A minimal metric

The example below is executed by
`tests/docs/test_admin_metrics_docs.py`. `Order` is any Tortoise model with a
`created_at` field.

```python
from flaxon.admin.metrics import Value

value = Value("Total orders", model=Order, range="30d", date_field="created_at")
dashboard.register_metric(value)
assert value.kind == "value"
```

`register_metric(metric, placement="dashboard")` places a card on the index.
Pass a registered model name to place it on that model's change list:

```python
dashboard.register_metric(value, placement="order")
assert value.placement == "order"
```

## The five metric kinds

Each class implements `calculate()` (SQL) and `render()` (inline SVG):

```python
from flaxon.admin.metrics import Partition, Progress, Table, Trend, Value

base = dict(model=Order, range="30d", date_field="created_at")
cards = [
    Value("Revenue", field="amount", aggregate="sum", **base),
    Trend("Orders per day", **base),
    Partition("Orders by status", field="status", **base),
    Progress("Fulfilled", current_filter={"fulfilled": True}, **base),
    Table("Top orders", columns=["reference", "amount"], limit=5, **base),
]
assert [card.kind for card in cards] == ["value", "trend", "partition", "progress", "table"]
```

The SVG from `render()` is offline and accessible. This is verified in a real
browser by `tests/browser/test_admin_metrics_browser.py`, which seeds a real
database and captures `assets/readme/admin-metrics.png`:

![Admin metrics dashboard](../assets/readme/admin-metrics.png)

## Ranges

`range` accepts `30d`, `60d`, `mtd`, `qtd`, `ytd` and `custom`. Ranges resolve to
UTC bounds that filter the SQL query.

```python
from datetime import datetime, timezone
from flaxon.admin.metrics import resolve_range

now = datetime(2026, 6, 15, 12, 0, 0, tzinfo=timezone.utc)
qtd = resolve_range("qtd", now=now)
assert qtd.start.month == 4 and qtd.start.day == 1

custom = resolve_range("custom", now=now, start=now, end=now)
assert custom.start == custom.end == now
```

## Caching and invalidation

`cached_calculate()` stores results for `ttl` seconds (default 60). Change a
card's data and call `dashboard.invalidate_metrics()` to refresh the cards.

```python
from flaxon.admin.metrics import TTLCache

cache = TTLCache()
cache.set("orders:value", 7, ttl=60)
assert cache.get("orders:value") == 7
assert cache.invalidate("orders:") == 1
assert cache.get("orders:value") is None
```

## Authorization

Every metric defaults to the `admin.view_dashboard` permission. Override it
with `permission="..."` to hide a card from users without that capability —
unauthorized users never see the card and no calculation runs.


---

# Source: docs/guides/admin-actions.md

# Admin actions

Flaxon Admin actions are reusable, class-based operations that an operator runs
from a model's change list: approve orders, export CSV, retry a job, and so on.
An `Action` bundles a label, prompt fields, a confirmation message, a scope,
authorization, an optional background mode, a result type and an audit entry.

Actions are **additive**: registration never changes the legacy
`register(Model, actions={...})` callables or the CMS `ContentType.register_action`
API. Every action runs behind CSRF protection and is capped by
`AdminConfig(action_bulk_limit=...)`.

## A minimal action

The example below is executed by `tests/docs/test_admin_actions_docs.py`.
`Order` is any registered model.

```python
from flaxon.admin.actions import Action, ActionResult, BULK

class MarkReviewed(Action):
    name = "mark_reviewed"
    label = "Mark reviewed"
    confirmation = "Mark the selected orders as reviewed?"
    scope = BULK

    async def handle(self, ids, params, context):
        return ActionResult.ok("Reviewed", data={"ids": list(ids)})

action = MarkReviewed()
dashboard.register_action(action, model=Order)
assert action.get_name() == "mark_reviewed"
assert action.scope == BULK
```

`register_action(action, model=...)` attaches the action to that model's action
selector and tracks it by name for background execution. Omit `model` to keep a
standalone action available only via the registry.

## Prompt fields and confirmation

Prompts ask the operator for input before an action runs. Values are validated
and coerced by `Prompt.clean()`; invalid input is rejected with HTTP 400 before
`handle()` runs. The `confirmation` text is shown in the browser's confirm
dialog.

```python
from flaxon.admin.actions import Prompt

prompts = [Prompt("mode", choices=("fast", "slow"), required=True)]
assert prompts[0].clean("fast") == "fast"
assert prompts[0].to_dict()["choices"] == ["fast", "slow"]
```

## The two shipped examples

`ApproveOrders` marks selected records as approved and reports failures per
record. `ExportCsv` downloads selected records as a spreadsheet-injection-safe
CSV (cells beginning with `=`, `+`, `-` or `@` are prefixed with `'`).

```python
from flaxon.admin.actions import ApproveOrders, ExportCsv

approve = ApproveOrders()
export = ExportCsv()
assert approve.name == "approve_orders"
assert export.name == "export_csv"
assert approve.to_schema()["confirmation"]
```

Both examples work end to end in `tests/integration/test_admin_actions_api.py`,
and the browser flow is captured from a real running app in
`tests/browser/test_admin_actions_browser.py`:

![Admin actions in a real browser](../assets/readme/admin-actions.png)

## Authorization and safety

Override `can_run()` for object-aware authorization. Returning `False` yields
HTTP 403 with no side effects. Legacy permission checks still apply, so access
is denied if either layer rejects the user.

```python
class ManagersOnly(MarkReviewed):
    name = "managers_only"
    permission = "order.managers_only_order"

    async def can_run(self, user, dashboard, **kwargs):
        return "manager" in getattr(user, "roles", [])

guarded = ManagersOnly()
assert guarded.permission == "order.managers_only_order"
```

Unauthorized users get 403 and no side effects; failures are reported per
record; bulk size is capped by `AdminConfig(action_bulk_limit=...)`; and each
run writes a full entry to the immutable audit log.

## Result types and background execution

`handle()` returns one of four result types:

| Result | Factory | Effect |
| --- | --- | --- |
| message | `ActionResult.ok("Done")` | Redirect back to the change list |
| redirect | `ActionResult.redirect(url)` | Redirect to a custom URL |
| download | `ActionResult.download(name, content)` | Stream a file attachment |
| danger | `ActionResult.danger("Failed", errors=[...])` | Report a failed result |

```python
from flaxon.admin.actions import ActionResult

assert ActionResult.ok("Done").kind == "message"
assert ActionResult.redirect("/admin/order").kind == "redirect"
assert ActionResult.download("x.csv", "a,b\n").kind == "download"
assert ActionResult.danger("Failed").kind == "danger"
```

Set `background = True` to enqueue the action onto the existing durable job
system instead of running it inline. The queued payload carries the action name,
model, ids and cleaned prompt values, and `dashboard.run_action_job(payload)`
executes it without an HTTP request.


---

# Source: docs/guides/admin-filters-and-safety.md

# Filters, lenses, discovery and safety

This guide covers the Phase 4 admin surface: declarative filters, lenses, saved
views, the command palette, record duplication, the CSV import wizard,
per-resource policies and impersonation.

Everything here is additive. A resource registered with the legacy
`dashboard.register(Model, list_filter=[...])` call keeps working exactly as
before; nothing below changes those defaults.

## Filters live in the URL

A filter is a small object that knows one field and one query-string key. The
change list renders a control for each declared filter, and the state is read
back from the URL, so a filtered list can be bookmarked, shared or saved.

```python
from flaxon.admin.filters import BooleanFilter, DateRangeFilter, SelectFilter, apply_python_filters

filters = [
    SelectFilter("status", choices=["pending", "paid"], label="Status"),
    BooleanFilter("fulfilled", label="Fulfilled"),
    DateRangeFilter("created_at", label="Created"),
]

params = {"filter_status": "paid", "filter_fulfilled": "true"}
rows = [
    {"id": 1, "status": "pending", "fulfilled": True},
    {"id": 2, "status": "paid", "fulfilled": False},
    {"id": 3, "status": "paid", "fulfilled": True},
]
selected = apply_python_filters(filters, params, rows)
```

`apply_python_filters` is the in-memory path used by legacy admin models. For
ORM-backed admins the same objects produce a Tortoise `Q` via `orm_q()`, and the
filter runs in SQL.

Register them on a resource:

```python
dashboard.register(
    Order,
    fields=["reference", "status", "fulfilled"],
    filters=[
        SelectFilter("status", choices=["pending", "paid"], label="Status"),
        BooleanFilter("fulfilled", label="Fulfilled"),
    ],
)
```

## Lenses: a second index for the same resource

A lens is a named alternate list with its own query and columns. It is addressed
by `?lens=<name>` and composes with filters and saved views.

```python
from flaxon.admin.lenses import Lens

unpaid = Lens(
    "unpaid",
    label="Unpaid orders",
    columns=["reference", "amount"],
    query={"filter_status": "pending"},
)
dashboard.register(Order, fields=["reference", "amount", "status"], lenses=[unpaid])
```

An unknown lens name is a `400`, not a silent fallback.

## Saved views are per-user query strings

A saved view stores the current query string under the signed-in user's name.
Applying it redirects to the list URL, so the URL stays the single source of
truth. Another user asking for the same slug gets `404` — saved views are not
enumerable.

## Discovery: command palette and shortcuts

`Ctrl`/`Cmd`+`K` opens the palette anywhere in the admin. It searches model
names and records the current user may read (`/admin/search/palette` returns
JSON). `Esc` closes it. The palette never returns records filtered out by a
`view` policy.

## Duplicate a record

`POST /admin/<model>/<id>/duplicate` copies a record with a fresh primary key.
It requires `create` permission, a valid CSRF token, and passes the record
through the resource's `create` policy.

## CSV import wizard

The import endpoint accepts CSV or JSON. Three additions make it a wizard:

* **Column mapping** — `?mapping={"Order Ref": "reference"}` renames source
  columns before validation.
* **Dry run** — `?dry_run=1` (or `?preview=1`) validates and returns the mapped
  rows without writing anything.
* **Caps** — `AdminConfig(import_max_rows=..., import_max_bytes=...)` rejects
  oversized payloads with `413`.

```python
from flaxon.admin.importing import csv_safe, enforce_limits, map_columns

mapped, errors = map_columns([{"Order Ref": "ORD-1"}], {"Order Ref": "reference"})
enforce_limits(payload_bytes=1024, row_count=len(mapped), max_bytes=5_000_000, max_rows=5000)
safe = csv_safe("=cmd|' /C calc'!A0")
```

Every CSV export passes values through `csv_safe`, which prefixes a single quote
to cells starting with `=`, `+`, `-`, `@`, tab or carriage return.

## Per-resource policies

A policy is deny-only. Actions you do not configure fall through to the existing
permission system, so adding a policy can only tighten access.

```python
from flaxon.admin.policies import Policy

policy = Policy(
    view_any=lambda user, obj=None: True,
    view=lambda user, obj=None: obj.get("status") != "archived",
    delete=lambda user, obj=None: False,
)
dashboard.register(Order, fields=["reference", "status"], policy=policy)
```

`view_any` gates the list, `view` is evaluated per record (an IDOR attempt on a
denied record returns `403`, not `404`-by-accident), and `create`, `update`,
`delete`, `restore` and `force_delete` gate the corresponding write paths.

## Impersonation is opt-in

```python
from flaxon.admin import AdminConfig, AdminDashboard

dashboard = AdminDashboard(
    app,
    config=AdminConfig(allow_impersonation=True),
    users=[
        {"username": "admin", "password": "Admin123!", "permissions": ["admin.superuser", "admin.impersonate"]},
        {"username": "viewer", "password": "Viewer123!", "permissions": ["admin.view_dashboard", "order.view_order"]},
    ],
)
```

Rules enforced server-side:

* Disabled unless `allow_impersonation=True`.
* The actor needs `admin.impersonate`.
* Superusers can never be impersonated.
* You cannot impersonate yourself.
* State is bound to the session token; logout ends it.
* Start and stop are both written to the audit log.

While active, every page shows a banner with a one-click **Exit impersonation**
button.


---

# Source: docs/guides/admin-extensions.md

# Admin extensions with Teloce

An admin extension adds **custom fields, dashboard cards, tools and pages** to the
Flaxon admin. The UI is written as Teloce `.vel` single-file components, which are
compiled by `teloce-py` — Python only. Extension authors never need Node.js, npm,
a bundler, or a CDN at build or run time.

Extensions ship as ordinary Python packages named `flaxon-admin-*` and are found
through the `flaxon.admin` entry-point group.

## What the admin does for you

- Compiles every `ui/*.vel` file once at startup and serves it from
  `<admin>/extensions/assets/<name>.js` as a same-origin ES module.
- Renders cards and pages on the server first, then mounts the component in the
  browser (progressive enhancement).
- Escapes every prop it writes into HTML, and keeps the admin's session,
  permission and CSRF rules for extension pages.
- Registers one dashboard card per model that uses your field, through the
  `model_registered` hook.

## Build a custom field in about 20 lines

A field is a `TeloceField`: a normal `Field` (so validation, sorting and
permissions still work) plus a component and a plain-HTML fallback. The component
receives `name`, `label`, `required` and the current `value` as props, and must
render a real control carrying the `name` prop so the form submits.

```python
from flaxon.admin import Component, TeloceField

SENTIMENT = """
<template>
  <fieldset :data-field="name"><legend>{{ label }}</legend>
    <label v-for="option in options" :key="option.value"><input type="radio" :name="name" :value="option.value" @change="pick(option.value)">{{ option.label }}</label>
  </fieldset>
</template>
<script lang="ts">
export default { props: { name: String, label: String, value: String, options: Array }, methods: { pick(value: string) { this.value = value; this.$emit("change", value); } } };
</script>
"""


class SentimentField(TeloceField):
    def __init__(self, name, **options):
        choices = [("happy", "Happy"), ("neutral", "Neutral"), ("sad", "Sad")]
        super().__init__(name, Component("sentiment", SENTIMENT), fallback="select", fallback_choices=choices, **options)


field = SentimentField("sentiment", label="How was it?")
assert field.schema_entry()["component"] == "sentiment"
```

Use it exactly like a built-in field:

```python
from flaxon.admin.resources import Resource, Text


class Feedback:
    """Your Tortoise model, shown here as a placeholder."""


class FeedbackResource(Resource):
    model = Feedback
    fields = [Text("comment"), SentimentField("sentiment").sortable()]
```

`fallback="select"` (or `"text"` / `"number"`) keeps the form usable before the
bundle mounts and when JavaScript is disabled. Validate the value in Python by
overriding `validation_field()` or passing `rules(...)`; the browser is never the
only guard.

## Cards, pages and tools

```python
from flaxon.admin import AdminExtension, Component, ExtensionPage, TeloceCard, Tool

CARD = """<template><p class="signups">{{ data.value }} signups</p></template>"""
PAGE = """<template><h2>{{ title }}</h2><p>{{ models.length }} models</p></template>"""


class SignupsCard(TeloceCard):
    def __init__(self, model):
        super().__init__("Signups", Component("signups", CARD), calculate=self.count, model=model)

    async def count(self, request=None, *, now=None):
        return {"value": await self.model.all().count()}


class ReportsPage(ExtensionPage):
    def __init__(self):
        super().__init__("reports", Component("reports", PAGE), permission="admin.view_reports")


class AnalyticsExtension(AdminExtension):
    name = "analytics"
    label = "Analytics"

    def setup(self, dashboard):
        dashboard.register_permission("admin.view_reports", "View reports", category="Extensions")

    def pages(self):
        return [ReportsPage()]

    def tools(self):
        return [Tool("Reports", ReportsPage(), icon="fa-chart-line")]
```

- `TeloceCard` calculates in Python (SQL through the ORM) and passes a
  JSON-serialisable dict as the `data` prop. Rendering happens in the component.
- `ExtensionPage` is mounted through `AdminDashboard.add_view`, so it keeps the
  permission check, CSRF check and navigation entry. Set an explicit
  `permission` — `admin.view_dashboard` is the default.
- `Tool` is a dashboard shortcut to a page. It does no work on the index, so
  adding tools cannot slow the dashboard down.
- `model_registered(dashboard, admin_model)` runs for models registered *after*
  the extension loaded. Use it to add per-model cards; that is how the example
  plugin adds one card per rated model.

## Discovery and configuration

```python
from flaxon.admin import AdminConfig

config = AdminConfig(disabled_extensions=("analytics",))
assert config.enable_extensions and config.disabled_extensions == ("analytics",)
```

Only distributions whose name starts with `flaxon-admin-` are auto-discovered;
other entry points in the `flaxon.admin` group are ignored with a warning. Pass
explicit instances with `AdminConfig(extensions=[AnalyticsExtension()])`, or turn
discovery off entirely with `AdminConfig(enable_extensions=False)`.

## Package it

```toml
[project]
name = "flaxon-admin-analytics"
version = "0.1.0"
dependencies = ["flaxon>=0.3.2", "teloce-py>=0.3.4"]

[project.entry-points."flaxon.admin"]
analytics = "flaxon_admin_analytics:AnalyticsExtension"

[tool.setuptools.package-data]
flaxon_admin_analytics = ["ui/*.vel"]
```

Place components in `<package>/ui/`; `AdminExtension.component("name.vel")` resolves
them and refuses paths outside the package.

## The complete example plugin

`examples/flaxon_admin_rating` is a working `flaxon-admin-rating` package:

```python
from flaxon_admin_rating import RatingExtension, RatingField

extension = RatingExtension()
assert extension.name == "rating"
assert RatingField("rating").component.name == "rating"
```

It contributes a 1–5 star `RatingField`, an average/distribution `RatingCard`, a
"Rating insights" page and a dashboard tool, and registers the
`admin.view_ratings` permission. Install and run it:

```bash
cd examples/flaxon_admin_rating
python -m pip install -e .
python -m flaxon run app:app --port 8000
```

Open `http://127.0.0.1:8000/admin/login` and sign in with `admin` / `Admin123!`.
The Products form shows the star control, the dashboard shows the card and tool,
and `/admin/ratings` lists every rated model.

## Limits worth knowing

- **Teloce's static renderer interpolates text and repeats `v-for` blocks, but it
  does not evaluate dynamic attribute bindings** (`:name`, `:checked`,
  `:data-x`). Cards and pages therefore use interpolated attributes; form fields
  rely on the HTML fallback until the component mounts. The browser bundle applies
  the real bindings.
- **Extensions are trusted code.** They run inside your process and can import
  anything. Discovery is restricted to `flaxon-admin-*` packages, but installing
  one is a deliberate act. There is no sandbox.
- **Assets are same-origin and authenticated.** The bundle and components require
  a signed-in user with `admin.view_dashboard`; nothing is fetched from a CDN.
- **Props are data, not markup.** Values are JSON-encoded and HTML-escaped before
  they reach an attribute, and Teloce renders text through text nodes.
- The extension bundle is one ES module per component plus a small loader. It is
  loaded on every admin page (cached with an `ETag`), so keep components small.

## Verify it

```bash
python -m pytest tests/unit/test_admin_extensions.py \
  tests/integration/test_admin_extensions_api.py \
  tests/browser/test_admin_extensions_browser.py -q --no-cov -o addopts=""
python scripts/generate_admin_extension_docs.py --check
```

The browser test drives the real admin under uvicorn: it logs in, checks the
server-rendered card, opens the extension page, clicks a star, submits the form,
and asserts the saved value — with no console errors and no external requests.

# Source: docs/guides/teloce-first-party-plugins.md

# Optional first-party plugins

These modules ship inside `teloce-py`, but builds include only modules you enable.
They work without Flaxon. They do not replace server validation, authorization,
SEO content rendered on the server, or an application-specific offline sync design.

## Configure a Flaxon application

```python
from flaxon import Flaxon

app = Flaxon("project-manager", debug=True)
app.use_teloce(
    ui_dir="ui",
    plugins={
        "forms": True,
        "i18n": {
            "locale": "en",
            "fallback": "en",
            "messages": {
                "en": {"welcome": "Welcome, {name}", "tasks": {"one": "{count} task", "other": "{count} tasks"}},
                "es": {"welcome": "Hola, {name}", "tasks": {"one": "{count} tarea", "other": "{count} tareas"}},
            },
        },
        "accessibility": True,
        "head": {
            "title": "Project manager",
            "description": "Manage projects and tasks",
            "pages": {"/projects": {"title": "Your projects", "description": "Your project dashboard"}},
        },
        "pwa": {
            "name": "Project manager",
            "short_name": "Projects",
            "start_url": "/",
            "scope": "/",
            "theme_color": "#0f172a",
            "icons": [
                {"src": "/static/icon-192.png", "sizes": "192x192", "type": "image/png"},
                {"src": "/static/icon-512.png", "sizes": "512x512", "type": "image/png"},
            ],
        },
    },
)
```

Provide real icon files at those URLs and mount their static directory. HTTPS (or
localhost) is required for service workers. PWA registration is disabled in development.
Browser installation eligibility depends on the manifest, icons and browser rules;
setting `pwa=True` alone does not guarantee an installation prompt.

Flaxon serves `/teloce-sw.js`, sets its allowed scope, adds the manifest link, initializes
plugins before mounting components, and connects Head/accessibility to its Teloce router.
Per-page `request.compile(..., meta={...})` overrides Head defaults in the initial HTML.
Omit a plugin, use `False`, or use `{"enabled": False}` to disable it. No extra pip package
is needed. This requires the matching new Teloce and Flaxon versions containing this integration.

## Forms

Browser modules are available as `globalThis.telocePlugins` after initialization.
The API is explicit: `v-model` updates component state; copy that value into the form
before submitting. Forms do not intercept requests or attach authentication headers.

```js
const { createForm, required, email, minLength } = globalThis.telocePlugins.forms;
const form = createForm(
  { email: "", password: "" },
  { email: [required, email], password: [required, minLength(8)] },
);
form.set("email", "person@example.com");
form.set("password", "example-password");
form.touch("email");

const unsubscribe = form.subscribe(() => {
  // Copy status into a component field or signal so its UI reacts.
  console.log(form.status.errors, form.status.submitting);
});

await form.submit(async values => {
  const response = await fetch("/api/login", {
    method: "POST",
    credentials: "same-origin",
    headers: { "content-type": "application/json" },
    body: JSON.stringify(values),
  });
  if (!response.ok) {
    form.setServerErrors(await response.json());
    return;
  }
  return response.json();
});
unsubscribe(); // Do this when the owning component unmounts.
```

`validate()` returns a boolean. Validation is synchronous; rules return an error string
or null. Duplicate submissions are ignored. Submission flags reset even when the handler
throws; catch failures in your UI. Values are plain structured-cloneable data.
`setServerErrors` accepts a field dictionary or an `errors`/`detail` array with `loc` or
`field` paths. Unknown paths become `_form` errors. `reset()` clears values, touched fields
and errors; resetting while submitting raises an error.

## Internationalization

```js
const i18n = globalThis.telocePlugins.i18n;
i18n.t("welcome", { name: "Aldane" });
i18n.t("tasks", { count: 2 });
i18n.number(1200, { style: "currency", currency: "JMD" });
i18n.date(new Date(), { dateStyle: "long" });
i18n.setLocale("es");
const unsubscribe = i18n.subscribe(() => {
  document.documentElement.lang = i18n.locale;
  // Update translated component fields/signals here.
});
```

Messages are text, not HTML. Named placeholders and `Intl.PluralRules` categories are
supported; this is not a full ICU MessageFormat parser. Missing translations use the
fallback locale, then the key. Subscriptions must be removed on component cleanup.

## Accessibility

```js
const a11y = globalThis.telocePlugins.accessibility;
a11y.announce("Task saved");
a11y.focus(document.querySelector("h1"));
const close = a11y.openDialog(document.querySelector("dialog"));
// Later:
close();
```

Use a labelled native `<dialog>` containing your normal buttons/forms. `showModal()`
provides browser keyboard containment and Escape handling; close restores focus to the
opener when it is still present. Router completion announces the current document title.
This does not supply missing labels, color contrast, or a complete accessible design.

## Head / SEO

```js
const head = globalThis.telocePlugins.head;
head.set({
  title: "Project: Website",
  description: "Tasks for your website project",
  canonical: "https://example.com/projects/website",
  ogTitle: "Website project",
  ogDescription: "A project dashboard",
  ogImage: "https://example.com/static/share.png",
});
```

`set` replaces the plugin-owned metadata using defaults plus the current page.
`og:title`, `og:description`, and `og:image` names are also accepted. URLs must be HTTP(S).
Tags are created with DOM APIs; strings are not injected as HTML. Router paths can map to
metadata through `head.pages`; dynamic projects call `set` after their data loads.
For discoverable content use SSR and Flaxon's per-page metadata; client-side tags alone
cannot guarantee crawler indexing.

## PWA updates and caching

```js
document.addEventListener("teloce:pwa-update", () => {
  // Show your own 'Update available' button.
});
const pwa = await globalThis.telocePlugins.pwa;
if (pwa?.updateAvailable) pwa.activateUpdate();
await pwa?.checkForUpdate();
```

Registration happens asynchronously and does not block application mounting. Unsupported
browsers return null; registration failures emit `teloce:pwa-error`. The update controller
has `registration`, `updateAvailable`, `checkForUpdate`, `activateUpdate` and `destroy`.
Activation is explicit, without an automatic refresh that could erase unfinished forms.
Reload after choosing to activate a waiting update. No install-prompt UI is supplied.

The worker precaches emitted JS/CSS and a generic offline page. It ignores non-GET requests,
cross-origin requests, query-bearing asset requests and all non-allowlisted API/data URLs.
Navigation stays network-first and is not cached; network failure shows the static offline
page. Sessions, Admin responses and private user data are never added by this worker.
Offline database edits, queues and conflict resolution are not provided. Cache cleanup is
namespaced by asset base and scope, and deletes only this application's old caches.

## Using another Python framework

```python
from teloce.build import build_project

result = build_project(".", "dist", options={
    "plugins": {"forms": True, "i18n": {"locale": "en"}},
    "public_path": "/static/",
})
```

Read `result["plugins"]["entry"]` (also in `manifest.json`), serve the output folder and
initialize plugins before mounting your component:

```js
import { installPlugins, connectPlugins } from "/static/teloce-plugins/index.js";
const plugins = await installPlugins();
// Mount your component/router here, then:
const disconnect = connectPlugins(plugins, router);
```

For PWA, also add a manifest link and serve the emitted worker at your configured
`workerURL` with an appropriate `Service-Worker-Allowed` header. Flaxon supplies those
steps automatically; other frameworks must do them explicitly. Runtime module factories
can also be imported directly from their emitted files for per-component instances.
Call instance cleanup methods and router disconnect functions when their owners unmount.


---

# Source: docs/api/application.md

# Application API

For generated projects, use the shared `settings.py`, `Flaxon.from_settings()`,
explicit mounts in `app.py`, and `management.py` workflow. See [ORM and project management](../guides/orm.md)
for Python migrations, model registration, permission hooks, relationship editing,
and Admin/CMS metadata storage. Backend-only and legacy adapter examples remain supported.

# Flaxon

The main application class.

---

## Constructor

```python
Flaxon(
    name: str,
    *,
    debug: bool | None = None,
    config: dict[str, Any] | None = None,
    openapi: bool | dict[str, Any] = False
)
```

### Parameters

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `name` | `str` | Application name |
| `debug` | `bool \| None` | Enable debug mode |
| `config` | `dict[str, Any] \| None` | Configuration dictionary |
| `openapi` | `bool \| dict[str, Any]` | Enable automatic OpenAPI, Swagger UI, and ReDoc. A mapping supplies `enable_openapi()` options. |

# Routing Methods

## route

```python
route(
    path: str,
    *,
    methods: set[str] | list[str] | tuple[str, ...] = ("GET",),
    name: str | None = None,
    summary: str | None = None,
    description: str | None = None,
    tags: list[str] | None = None,
    operation_id: str | None = None,
    responses: dict[str | int, Any] | None = None,
    deprecated: bool = False,
    security: list[dict[str, list[str]]] | None = None
) -> Callable
```

Register a route with custom HTTP methods.

The `get`, `post`, `put`, `patch`, and `delete` helpers accept the same
OpenAPI metadata: `summary`, `description`, `tags`, `operation_id`,
`responses`, `deprecated`, and `security`.

See the [OpenAPI guide](../guides/openapi.md) for query parameters, schemas,
guards, and CLI validation.

# OpenAPI Methods

## enable_openapi

```python
enable_openapi(
    title: str = "Flaxon API",
    version: str = "1.0.0",
    description: str | None = None,
    openapi_url: str = "/openapi.json",
    docs_url: str | None = "/docs",
    redoc_url: str | None = "/redoc",
    include_internal: bool = False,
    docs_guard: Callable[[Request], Any] | None = None,
    protect_docs: bool = False,
    persist_authorization: bool = False,
    swagger_asset_url: str | None = None,
    redoc_asset_url: str | None = None,
) -> Any
```

Register the generated OpenAPI JSON endpoint and interactive Swagger UI and
ReDoc pages. By default (`swagger_asset_url=None`, `redoc_asset_url=None`) Flaxon
serves the Swagger UI and ReDoc files that ship with it, so both pages work
offline; pass a URL to use your own copy. This is equivalent to passing `openapi=True` or an options mapping
to the constructor. See the [OpenAPI guide](../guides/openapi.md).

## add_lifespan_context

```python
add_lifespan_context(
    factory: Callable[[], AbstractAsyncContextManager[Any]]
) -> Callable[[], AbstractAsyncContextManager[Any]]
```

Register an async context manager for a mounted ASGI application's startup and
shutdown lifecycle. Contexts are entered before startup callbacks and exited
after shutdown callbacks. FastMCP integrations use this method to initialize
and close MCP session managers correctly.

# Request

## Constructor

```python

    scope: dict[str, Any],
    receive: Any,

)
```

---

## Properties

| Property | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `method` | `str` | HTTP method |
| `path` | `str` | Request path |
| `root_path` | `str` | Root path |
| `scheme` | `str` | URL scheme |
| `headers` | `Headers` | Request headers |
| `path_params` | `dict[str, Any]` | Path parameters |
| `state` | `SimpleNamespace` | Request state |
| `user` | `Any` | Authenticated user |
| `query` | `QueryParams` | Query parameters |
| `cookies` | `Cookies` | Cookies |
| `client` | `tuple[str, int] \| None` | Client address |
| `host` | `str` | Host header |
| `url` | `str` | Full URL |

| regex      | re.Pattern | Compiled route regex  |
| parameters | list[str]  | Route parameter names |

# Source: docs/api/validation.md

# Validation API

## Schema

Base schema class for data validation.

### Constructor

```python
class Schema(metaclass=SchemaMeta):
    __fields__: dict[str, Field]
````

---

## Class Methods

### load

```python
@classmethod
def load(cls, data: Any) -> Schema
```

Load and validate data from a dictionary.

| Parameter | Type | Description                             |
| --------- | ---- | --------------------------------------- |
| data      | Any  | Data to validate (must be a dictionary) |

**Raises:**

`ValidationError` if validation fails.

**Returns:**

A schema instance with validated data.

Example:

```python
user = CreateUser.load({
    "name": "Alice",
    "email": "alice@example.com"
})
```

---

## Methods

### to_dict

```python
def to_dict(self) -> dict[str, Any]
```

Convert schema to a dictionary.

Example:

```python
data = user.to_dict()

# {
#   "name": "Alice",
#   "email": "alice@example.com"
# }
```

### to_json

```python
def to_json(self) -> dict[str, Any]
```

Convert schema to a JSON serializable dictionary.

Example:

```python
json_data = user.to_json()
```

### validate

```python
def validate(self) -> None
```

Validate schema data manually.

**Raises:**

`ValidationError` if validation fails.

---

# Fields

## StrField

String field with validation options.

```python
StrField(
    *,
    required: bool = False,
    default: Any = None,
    nullable: bool = False,
    min_length: int | None = None,
    max_length: int | None = None,
    strip: bool = True,
    pattern: str | None = None,
)
```

| Parameter  | Type       | Description              |
| ---------- | ---------- | ------------------------ |
| required   | bool       | Field must be present    |
| default    | Any        | Default value if missing |
| nullable   | bool       | Allow null values        |
| min_length | int | None | Minimum string length    |
| max_length | int | None | Maximum string length    |
| strip      | bool       | Remove whitespace        |
| pattern    | str | None | Regex pattern            |

Example:

```python
name = fields.StrField(
    required=True,
    min_length=2,
    max_length=80
)
```

---

## IntField

Integer field with range validation.

```python
IntField(
    *,
    required: bool = False,
    default: Any = None,
    nullable: bool = False,
    minimum: int | None = None,
    maximum: int | None = None,
)
```

| Parameter | Type       | Description           |
| --------- | ---------- | --------------------- |
| minimum   | int | None | Minimum allowed value |
| maximum   | int | None | Maximum allowed value |

Example:

```python
age = fields.IntField(
    minimum=13,
    maximum=120
)
```

---

```python
FloatField(

    maximum: float | None = None,
```

## ListField

List field with item validation.

```python
ListField(
    item_field: Field | None = None,
    *,
    required: bool = False,
    default: Any = None,
    nullable: bool = False,
    min_items: int | None = None,
    max_items: int | None = None,
)
```

| Parameter  | Type         | Description                |
| ---------- | ------------ | -------------------------- |
| item_field | Field | None | Validation field for items |
| min_items  | int | None   | Minimum items              |
| max_items  | int | None   | Maximum items              |

Example:

```python

    fields.StrField(min_length=1),
    min_items=1,
    max_items=10
)
```

---

## NestedField

Nested schema field.

```python
NestedField(
    schema_class: type[Schema],
    *,
    required: bool = False,
    default: Any = None,
    nullable: bool = False,
)
```

Example:

```python
class AddressSchema(Schema):
    street = fields.StrField(required=True)
    city = fields.StrField(required=True)


class UserSchema(Schema):
    name = fields.StrField(required=True)
    address = fields.NestedField(AddressSchema)
```

---

## AnyField

Accepts any value.

```python
AnyField(
    *,
    required: bool = False,
    default: Any = None,
    nullable: bool = False,
)
```

Example:

```python
metadata = fields.AnyField()
```

# Exceptions

## ValidationError

Raised when validation fails.

```python
ValidationError(
    fields: dict[str, list[str]]
)
```

| Attribute | Type                 | Description          |
| --------- | -------------------- | -------------------- |
| fields    | dict[str, list[str]] | Field error messages |

Example:

```python
try:
    user = CreateUser.load(data)

except ValidationError as exc:
    print(exc.fields)
```

---

## FieldError

Raised when a field validation fails.

```python
FieldError(message: str)
```

| Attribute | Type | Description   |
| --------- | ---- | ------------- |
| message   | str  | Error message |

---

# Complete Example

```python
from flaxon.validation import Schema, fields
from flaxon.validation.validators import (
    custom_validator,
    and_validators,
    pattern_validator,
)


def validate_unique_email(value, field):
    if value == "admin@example.com":
        raise FieldError("Email already registered")


class CreateUser(Schema):
    username = fields.StrField(
        required=True,
        min_length=3,
        max_length=30,
        validators=[
            and_validators(
                pattern_validator(
                    r"^[a-zA-Z0-9_]+$"
                )
            )
        ],
    )

    email = fields.EmailField(
        required=True,
        validators=[
            custom_validator(validate_unique_email)
        ],
    )

    password = fields.StrField(
        required=True,
        min_length=8,
        max_length=128,
    )

    age = fields.IntField(
        required=False,
        minimum=13,
        maximum=120,
    )

    role = fields.ChoiceField(
        ["user", "moderator", "admin"],
        default="user",
    )

    tags = fields.ListField(
        fields.StrField(min_length=1),
        max_items=10,
    )


@app.post("/users")
async def create_user(data: CreateUser):
    return {
        "user": data.to_dict()
    }
```


## Use this capability in a full-stack app

Flaxon serves Python APIs and Teloce interfaces in one project. Keep validation,
authorization and privileged operations on the server; components call those
endpoints and present their results. Follow the [full-stack lessons](../fullstack/index.md)
and [Teloce integration reference](../api/teloce.md) to connect this capability
to pages, components and application modules.


---

# WebSocket API

## WebSocket

WebSocket connection handler.

### Constructor

```python
WebSocket(
    scope: dict[str, Any],
    receive: Any,
    send: Any,
    manager: Any = None
)
````

### Properties

| Property      | Type             | Description                              |
| ------------- | ---------------- | ---------------------------------------- |
| `path_params` | `dict[str, Any]` | Path parameters                          |
| `state`       | `WebSocketState` | Connection state                         |
| `accepted`    | `bool`           | Whether the connection has been accepted |
| `closed`      | `bool`           | Whether the connection has been closed   |

---

## Methods

### accept

```python
async def accept(
    subprotocol: str | None = None,
    headers: list[tuple[bytes, bytes]] | None = None
) -> None
```

Accept the WebSocket connection.

---

### receive

```python
async def receive() -> dict[str, Any]
```

Receive a WebSocket message.

---

### receive_text

```python
async def receive_text() -> str
```

Receive a text message.

---

### receive_bytes

```python
async def receive_bytes() -> bytes
```

Receive a binary message.

---

### receive_json

```python
async def receive_json() -> Any
```

Receive a JSON message.

---

### send_text

```python
async def send_text(value: str) -> None
```

Send a text message.

---

### send_bytes

```python
async def send_bytes(value: bytes) -> None
```

Send a binary message.

---

### send_json

```python
async def send_json(value: Any) -> None
```

Send a JSON message.

---

### close

```python
async def close(code: int = 1000, reason: str = "") -> None
```

Close the WebSocket connection.

---

### join

```python
async def join(room: str) -> None
```

Join a room.

---

### leave

```python
async def leave(room: str) -> None
```

Leave a room.

---

### broadcast_json

```python
async def broadcast_json(room: str, value: Any) -> None
```

Broadcast JSON data to all connections in a room.

---

### broadcast_text

```python
async def broadcast_text(room: str, value: str) -> None
```

Broadcast text data to all connections in a room.

### iter_json

```python
def iter_json(self) -> AsyncIterator[Any]
```

Iterate over incoming JSON messages.

### iter_text

```python

```

# WebSocketState

WebSocket connection states.

| Value        | Description |
| ------------ | ----------- |
| `CONNECTING` | Connecting  |
| `CONNECTED`  | Connected   |
| `CLOSING`    | Closing     |
| `CLOSED`     | Closed      |


Flaxon serves Python APIs and Teloce interfaces in one project. Keep validation,
authorization and privileged operations on the server; components call those
endpoints and present their results. Follow the [full-stack lessons](../fullstack/index.md)
and [Teloce integration reference](../api/teloce.md) to connect this capability
to pages, components and application modules.

## Production Services

These services are available for durable Admin integrations:

```python
from flaxon.admin import (
    DurableJobStore, DurableJobWorker, ImmutableAuditLog,
    NotificationService, ResumableUploadStore, WebAuthnService,
)
```

| Service | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `DurableJobStore` | Persist queued, running, completed, and failed jobs with retry metadata. |
| `DurableJobWorker` | Register named handlers and process due jobs. |
| `ImmutableAuditLog` | Append hash-chained records and verify tamper evidence. |
| `NotificationService` | Store preferences and per-user channel delivery records. |
| `ResumableUploadStore` | Persist upload sessions, chunks, and final SHA-256 validation. |
| `WebAuthnService` | Delegate registration and assertion ceremonies to an injected provider. |

## HTTP Endpoints

| Method | Path | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `POST` | `/admin/media/resumable` | Create a resumable upload session. |
| `GET` | `/admin/media/resumable/{upload_id}` | Read the current upload offset and expiry. |
| `PATCH` | `/admin/media/resumable/{upload_id}` | Upload a raw byte chunk using `Upload-Offset`. |
| `POST` | `/admin/media/resumable/{upload_id}/complete` | Validate and persist the completed upload. |
| `GET` | `/admin/media/folders` | List configured media folders. |
| `POST` | `/admin/media/folders` | Create a media folder with a CSRF header. |
| `DELETE` | `/admin/media/folders/{folder}` | Delete a folder and its stored files. |
| `POST` | `/admin/media/bulk` | Delete selected media names with a CSRF header. |
| `PATCH` | `/admin/media/{filename}` | Rename an asset or update allowed metadata. |
| `DELETE` | `/admin/media/{filename}` | Delete one asset with a CSRF header. |
| `GET` | `/admin/media/{filename}/signed-url` | Return a storage signed URL when the adapter supports it. |
| `GET` | `/admin/notifications/preferences` | Read the current user’s notification preferences. |
| `POST` | `/admin/notifications/preferences` | Update preferences with a CSRF header. |
| `GET` | `/admin/audit/verify` | Verify the persisted audit hash chain. |
| `POST` | `/admin/profile/webauthn/register/begin` | Start provider-backed credential registration. |
| `POST` | `/admin/profile/webauthn/register/finish` | Complete credential registration. |
| `POST` | `/admin/profile/webauthn/authenticate/begin` | Start provider-backed authentication. |
| `POST` | `/admin/profile/webauthn/authenticate/finish` | Verify an authentication assertion. |
| `GET` | `/admin/profile/trusted-devices` | List the signed-in user's trusted devices. |
| `POST` | `/admin/profile/trusted-devices` | Issue one opaque trusted-device token after MFA. |
| `DELETE` | `/admin/profile/trusted-devices/{device_id}` | Revoke one trusted device. |
| `POST` | `/admin/profile/mfa/recovery-codes` | Rotate MFA recovery codes and revoke trusted devices. |
| `GET` | `/admin/cms/api/scheduler/jobs` | Inspect durable scheduled-publication jobs. |
| `POST` | `/admin/cms/api/scheduler/jobs/{job_id}/retry` | Requeue a failed scheduled-publication job. |
| `GET` | `/admin/cms/api/media` | List reusable Admin media for CMS fields. |

All authenticated Admin mutations require the session cookie and
`X-CSRF-Token`. Use `redis_url` for shared sessions, rate limits, and
multi-worker coordination.

## Authorization

```python
from flaxon.admin import (
    AsyncAuthorizationProvider,
    CasbinAuthorizationProvider,
    DefaultAuthorizationProvider,
    PermissionCatalog,
    RedisPolicySynchronizer,
    default_group_definitions,
)
```

`PermissionCatalog` exposes readable definitions for model `view`, `add`,
`change`, and `delete` actions plus CMS capabilities. `DefaultAuthorizationProvider`
is dependency-free and supports legacy aliases during migration. Set
`strict_permissions=True` on `AdminDashboard` to require exact capabilities.
`CasbinAuthorizationProvider` is an optional adapter for an application-owned
PyCasbin enforcer; Casbin is not a Flaxon runtime dependency.

Use `default_group_definitions()` to seed the named `Administrator`, `Content
Editor`, `Publisher`, `Media Manager`, `Warehouse Staff`, `Support Agent`, and
`Read Only` groups. The legacy `staff` and `editor` names remain available for
migrations. A provider may implement async `has_permission`; Admin awaits it
at every protected request boundary. `RedisPolicySynchronizer` publishes
policy-change events and calls the enforcer's `load_policy()` in every worker.

## Optional production dependencies

Install the feature groups explicitly:

```shell
pip install "flaxon[admin,policy,scheduler]"
```

The `admin` group adds `nh3`, Pillow, `python-magic`, Argon2, and WebAuthn;
`policy` adds PyCasbin; `scheduler` adds APScheduler. `python-magic` also
requires the platform's libmagic runtime. `bandit` and `pip-audit` are part of
the development tools for CI security checks.

## Microservice control plane

The control plane is enabled by default when `AdminDashboard` is created. The
JSON API is rooted at `/admin/api/control-plane/` and the browser pages use
the same persistent records.

```python
from flaxon.admin import (
    AdminControlPlane,
    RemoteModelAdapter,
    RemoteServiceClient,
    ServiceRegistry,
)
```

# Admin extension API

Generated from `flaxon.admin.extensions` by `scripts/generate_admin_extension_docs.py`.
Do not edit by hand: run the script (or `python scripts/generate_admin_extension_docs.py --check`).

## `ADMIN_EXTENSION_GROUP`

Constant: `flaxon.admin`.

## `AdminExtension`

`class AdminExtension(*, root: str | pathlib.Path | None = None) -> None`

Base class for a ``flaxon-admin-*`` package.

### `bind`

`bind(dashboard: Any) -> None`

Attach the extension to a dashboard (called once by the registry).

### `cards`

`cards() -> list[metrics.Metric]`

Return dashboard cards contributed by this extension.

### `component`

`component(filename: str) -> Component`

Return (and cache) the component stored in ``ui/<filename>``.

### `components`

`components() -> list[Component]`

Return every component in ``ui/`` plus any declared out of tree.

### `fields`

`fields() -> list[type[resources.Field]]`

Return custom field classes contributed by this extension.

### `model_registered`

`model_registered(dashboard: Any, admin_model: Any) -> None`

Called when a model is registered after the extension was loaded.

### `pages`

`pages() -> list[ExtensionPage]`

Return custom admin pages contributed by this extension.

### `setup`

`setup(dashboard: Any) -> None`

Optional hook for permissions or other registration work.

### `tools`

`tools() -> list[Tool]`

Return tools shown on the admin dashboard.

## `Component`

`class Component(name: str, source: str | pathlib.Path) -> None`

One ``.vel`` single-file component owned by an extension.

### `compile`

`compile() -> str`

Compile the component to a JavaScript ES module (cached).

### `mount_point`

`mount_point(props: dict[str, typing.Any] | None = None, *, value: Any = None, body: str = ) -> str`

Return the escaped mount element the browser bundle enhances.

### `render`

`render(props: dict[str, typing.Any] | None = None) -> str`

Render the component to HTML on the server (no browser script runs).

## `EXTENSION_DISTRIBUTION_PREFIX`

Constant: `flaxon-admin-`.

## `ExtensionError`

`class ExtensionError`

Raised when an admin extension cannot be loaded or compiled.

## `ExtensionPage`

`class ExtensionPage(name: str, component: Component, *, label: str | None = None, url: str | None = None, permission: str = admin.view_dashboard, icon: str = fa-puzzle-piece, category: str = Extensions, description: str = , props: Any = None, methods: set[str] | None = None) -> None`

A custom admin page rendered from a Teloce component.

### `bind`

`bind(dashboard: Any) -> None`

Remember the dashboard used by :meth:`handler`.

### `build_props`

`build_props(request: Any) -> dict[str, typing.Any]`

Evaluate the page's props for ``request`` (sync or async callables).

### `handler`

`handler(request: Any) -> Any`

Render the page through the dashboard's Jinax environment.

## `ExtensionRegistry`

`class ExtensionRegistry(dashboard: Any) -> None`

Owns extension discovery, validation, compilation and asset serving.

### `asset_url`

`asset_url(name: str) -> str`

Return the admin-relative URL of one compiled component.

### `build`

`build() -> None`

Compile every component once; fail early on a broken extension.

### `bundle`

`bundle() -> str`

Return the ES module that mounts every component on the page.

### `code`

`code(name: str) -> str`

Return the compiled JavaScript for a component.

### `component`

`component(name: str) -> Component`

Return a registered component by name.

### `load`

`load(*, include: collections.abc.Iterable[AdminExtension] | None = None) -> list[AdminExtension]`

Discover ``flaxon-admin-*`` entry points and register the results.

### `register`

`register(extension: AdminExtension) -> AdminExtension`

Bind and register one extension; contributions are added immediately.

## `TeloceCard`

`class TeloceCard(title: str, component: Component, *, calculate: Any, props: Any = None, **options: Any) -> None`

A dashboard card whose markup is a Teloce component.

### `calculate`

`calculate(request: Any = None, *, now: Any = None) -> dict[str, typing.Any]`

Return the card data, awaiting the callable when needed.

### `render`

`render(data: dict[str, typing.Any]) -> str`

Render the component on the server and return its mount point.

## `TeloceField`

`class TeloceField(name: str, component: Component, *, props: dict[str, typing.Any] | None = None, fallback: str = text, fallback_choices: collections.abc.Iterable[tuple[typing.Any, str]] = (), **options: Any) -> None`

A form field whose control is a Teloce component.

### `props_for`

`props_for(value: Any = None) -> dict[str, typing.Any]`

Return the props passed to the component for ``value``.

### `schema_entry`

`schema_entry() -> dict[str, typing.Any]`

Expose the component and its static props to the field template.

## `Tool`

`class Tool(label: str, page: ExtensionPage, *, icon: str = fa-toolbox, description: str = , permission: str | None = None) -> None`

A dashboard shortcut contributed by an extension.

## `load_extensions`

`load_extensions(*, group: str = flaxon.admin, disabled: collections.abc.Iterable[str] = (), entry_points: Any = None) -> list[AdminExtension]`

Load extensions from installed ``flaxon-admin-*`` distributions.

# Source: docs/api/teloce.md

# Teloce full-stack integration: API reference

Flaxon owns HTTP, APIs and WebSockets. Teloce compiles UI components and handles
browser state and navigation. MinifyJS optimizes generated production JavaScript;
it does not execute requests or replace Teloce's compiler.

## API reference

### `app.use_teloce(...)`

Register once, before application startup. Returns `Teloce` and exposes it as
`app.teloce`.

| Argument | Default | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `project_root` | Current directory | Root containing every UI source |
| `ui_dir` | `ui` | Application components and pages |
| `build_dir` | `.flaxon/build` | Generated output, relative to project root |
| `static_url` | `/_flaxon` | Browser URL serving generated files |
| `entry` | `app.html` | Root component within a registered UI tree |
| `title` | Application name | HTML document title |
| `options` | `{}` | Overrides passed to Teloce Builder; also `spa_mode`/`spa_base` |

Startup compiles sources. Missing directories, invalid components and duplicate
page routes fail the build. UI directories must be within `project_root`.

### `await request.compile(entry="app.html", context=None, title=None)`

Returns an `HTMLResponse` shell importing the root component, styles and router.
Context is safely serialized as JSON and passed to `mount()`. This is client-side
rendering, not server-rendered component HTML. A cached startup build is reused;
if none exists, the integration builds lazily. Configure `app.use_teloce()` first.
Never put secrets in context: it is visible in the browser.

### `app.teloce.build()` and `register_source(name, directory, routes=None)`

`build()` explicitly rebuilds registered trees and returns Teloce's result.
`register_source()` adds a source and invalidates the cached build. Names and
source directories must be unique. Register before serving traffic; runtime
concurrent builds are not a deployment strategy.

### `FlaxonModule(name, ui_dir=..., ui_routes=...)`

Mounting a module registers its backend endpoints and UI source. It works before
or after `use_teloce()`. `ui_routes` maps generated page filenames to client paths,
for example `{"ProductDetails/[id].js": "/products/:id"}`. Backend mount prefixes
such as `/api/catalog` do not automatically prefix browser page routes.

### Navigation attributes

`data-teloce-router-view` identifies the page outlet (or use `id="router-view"`).
`data-teloce-link` marks an anchor for client navigation:

```html
<a href="/jobs" data-teloce-link>Jobs</a>
<main data-teloce-router-view></main>
```

The listener only intercepts ordinary same-origin HTTP(S) clicks to a matching
client route. External links, modified clicks, downloads, other targets,
nonmatching routes and same-page fragments retain browser behavior. Router guards
can reject a matched navigation; it does not fall back to a full page load.
The server still needs a catch-all route for direct visits and page refreshes.

## Lesson 1: Compile your first interface

Install `flaxon[standard]` and a Teloce version containing its MinifyJS integration.
For repository development, install Flaxon and updated Teloce from their actual
local checkouts; do not copy another developer's Windows path.

Create `ui/app.html`:

```html
<template><h1>{{ business }}</h1></template>
<script>export default { props: ["business"] };</script>
```

Create `app.py`:

```python
from pathlib import Path
from flaxon import Flaxon, Request

app = Flaxon("My business", debug=True)
app.use_teloce(project_root=Path(__file__).parent, ui_dir="ui")

@app.get("/")
async def home(request: Request):
    return await request.compile("app.html", {"business": "Morgan Build & Repair"})
```

Run `flaxon run app:app --reload` and visit port 8000. The component is compiled
as HTML-mode Teloce input, not served as raw HTML. `.vel` components are also
supported by Teloce. Edit a source and refresh after the server restarts.
Generated `.flaxon` files are excluded from the watcher; `.vel` files are included.
This process reload is not browser HMR.

## Lesson 2: Load data from Flaxon

Add an API before your catch-all route:

```python
@app.get("/api/jobs")
async def jobs():
    return {"items": [{"id": 1, "customer": "Harbour View Bakery"}]}
```

A page can fetch it after mounting:

```html
<template><p v-for="job in jobs" :key="job.id">{{ job.customer }}</p></template>
<script>
export default {
  data() { return { jobs: [] }; },
  async mounted() {
    const response = await fetch("/api/jobs");
    if (!response.ok) throw new Error("Could not load jobs");
    this.jobs = (await response.json()).items;
  }
};
</script>
```

The shipped SiteLedger Jobs page adds loading state, a Refresh button and a
reusable `JobCard`. Its in-memory API is a teaching fixture: add persistence,
authorization and visible loading/error states for production.

## Lesson 3: Add page navigation

Put pages in `ui/pages/`; `Jobs.html` becomes `/jobs` and `jobs/[id].html` becomes
`/jobs/:id`. Put marked links and a router outlet in `app.html`.
Add a server fallback after API routes:

```python
@app.get("/")
@app.get("/<path:spa_path>")
async def page(request: Request, spa_path: str = ""):
    return await request.compile("app.html", {"business": "My business"})
```

The browser router mounts pages; Flaxon handles `/api/...` data. Directly visiting
`/jobs/1` returns the same shell, and the router reads the URL. SiteLedger's detail
page receives `id` as a prop and fetches `/api/jobs/${this.id}`.

## Lesson 4: Keep a feature in one module

```python
from pathlib import Path
from flaxon.modules import FlaxonModule

catalog = FlaxonModule(
    "catalog", ui_dir=Path(__file__).parent / "ui",
    ui_routes={"ProductDetails/[id].js": "/products/:id"},
)

@catalog.get("/products")
async def products():
    return {"items": []}

# In the application:
app.mount_module(catalog, prefix="/api/catalog")
```

See the modules shop for auth, catalog, orders and chat. Catalog owns pages and
product components; chat owns a WebSocket and its page. Its browser component
closes the socket in `beforeUnmount()`. Duplicate page routes across modules fail
rather than silently choosing one. The sample login/data are demonstrations,
not a complete security or database implementation.

## Lesson 5: Deploy with MinifyJS

Use `debug=False`. Flaxon requests production compilation, asset hashes and
extracted CSS. Updated Teloce uses MinifyJS for component/runtime optimization;
Flaxon also optimizes its separately generated router through MinifyJS. Both
compression and local-name mangling are enabled for that router. No Node is needed.

Development keeps Teloce's existing pipeline and source maps. This change does
not enable the experimental native development backend. Bundling is not enabled
by default; it requires selecting an appropriate entry and testing all module
pages/lazy imports. Do not assume the startup integration is a unified bundle.

The build directory is served with `Cache-Control: no-cache` in both modes, so
stable aliases and `router.js` revalidate after deployment. The HTML shell uses
`no-cache` in production and `no-store` in development. A CDN must preserve this
policy; only add long immutable caching to files with verified content hashes.

Install pinned compatible versions, build in a writable location at startup,
and deploy source plus dependencies (or arrange an explicit build lifecycle).
Each worker currently builds on startup: avoid concurrent writes to a shared
build directory by using a single builder or isolated worker output directories.
Add real authentication, database storage and authorization for business data.

[SiteLedger example](../../examples/teloce_siteledger/README.md) ·
[Modules example](../../examples/teloce_modules_shop/README.md)

## Optional page-head configuration

All additions are optional; existing `title`-only applications continue working.

```python
app.mount_static("/static", str(project_root / "public"))
theme_cdn = "https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap@5.3.3/dist/css/bootstrap.min.css"
app.use_teloce(
    project_root=project_root, ui_dir="ui", title="Taskboard",
    favicon="/static/favicon.svg", description="Team tasks in one place.",
    lang="en", theme_color="#101827", stylesheets=[theme_cdn],
    scripts=[{"src": "/static/help.js", "defer": True}],
)
```

| Option | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `favicon` | None | Icon link URL; serve the file separately |
| `description` | None | Escaped description meta content |
| `lang` | `en` | Escaped HTML document language, not script language |
| `theme_color` | None | Theme-color meta content |
| `stylesheets` | None | Ordered strings or dictionaries containing `href` |
| `scripts` | None | Ordered strings or dictionaries containing `src` |

Scripts support `type`, boolean `defer`/`async`, `integrity`, `crossorigin`,
`referrerpolicy`. Stylesheets support `rel`, `type`, `media`, `sizes`, `integrity`,
`crossorigin`, `referrerpolicy`. Resource URLs allow relative, HTTP and HTTPS
URLs; executable/data schemes and unknown attributes are rejected. Values are
escaped; arbitrary HTML/event-handler attributes are not accepted.

These settings add tags to the head; they do not download, bundle or upload CDN
resources. Pin trusted dependencies. Scripts execute with page privileges.
Use verified SRI hashes and `crossorigin="anonymous"` where supported; don't
invent hashes. Async resources have no guaranteed execution order. Do not assume
an external library has loaded before a component mounts: coordinate explicitly
if your component depends on it. Fonts and resources may require network access
and disclose requests to providers. Local copies support offline applications.

Generated component CSS precedes extra stylesheet links, allowing intentional
external overrides. Deferred classic scripts retain their order with each other;
module and async timing needs separate consideration. The integration still
emits an inline module bootstrap; a strict CSP needs a compatible nonce/hash
strategy beyond these resource attributes. A favicon does not configure native
Windows icons. Manifest and arbitrary head HTML are not part of this API.

For TypeScript, use `<script lang="ts">` and import `.ts` helpers with a compatible
Teloce version. Output is JavaScript; transpilation does not replace type checking.
See the [tested example](../../examples/teloce_head_ts/README.md) and
[10 full-stack lessons](../fullstack/index.md).


## SSR and metadata options

`await request.compile(entry, public_props, ssr=True, meta={...})` renders a
manifest-linked AST program and hydrates the same public snapshot. `meta`
supports title, description, canonical, Open Graph title/description/image/url/type,
and `twitter:card`; values are escaped and resource URLs are validated.

Use `options={"ssr": "opt-in", "ssr_entries": ["app.html"]}` for selected pages.
`ssr_fallback` defaults to `"error"`; `"client"` explicitly allows render-error
fallback. `ssr_cache_size` enables bounded rendering cache; default is zero.
Read [SSR and browser debugging](../guides/teloce-ssr-debugging.md) for the
supported syntax, public-data rules, diagnostics, and production boundaries.

## Build the generated starter for production

```bash
python management.py build
```

This command forces a production Teloce build with MinifyJS bundling and
minification, extracted scoped CSS, hashed assets, and no development source
maps or debugger client. It includes the UI contributed by mounted modules.
Compilation errors exit unsuccessfully so deployment stops.

In `app.py`, call `app.use_teloce(...)` after mounting modules and before the
`if app.is_management: return app` guard. Keep database connections and Admin
store initialization after that guard. `build` does not run startup hooks or
apply migrations. Backend-only projects do not need this command.

## Automatic development rebuilds

Run `python management.py runserver` with `DEBUG=True`. Saved `.html`, `.vel`,
`.ts`, `.tsx`, `.js`, `.jsx`, `.css`, and `.json` changes inside registered application
and module UI folders are detected by the development browser every two seconds.
Flaxon rebuilds the UI once and refreshes open pages after a successful build.
Compilation failures show a notice linking to the debugger; another saved edit retries.

This is automatic rebuilding and full-page reload, not state-preserving component HMR.
Unsaved editor changes are not visible; enable your editor's Auto Save if desired.
Python changes still use the development server's Python reload. Imported files outside
registered UI roots are not watched. Production registers no reload endpoint or client.

## Optional first-party modules

Configure these in `app.use_teloce(plugins={...})`:

```python
app.use_teloce(ui_dir="ui", plugins={
    "forms": True,
    "i18n": {"locale": "en", "messages": {"en": {"welcome": "Welcome"}}},
    "accessibility": True,
    "head": {"title": "Tasks", "pages": {"/projects": {"title": "Projects"}}},
    "pwa": {"name": "Tasks", "scope": "/", "icons": [
        {"src": "/static/icon-192.png", "sizes": "192x192", "type": "image/png"},
        {"src": "/static/icon-512.png", "sizes": "512x512", "type": "image/png"},
    ]},
})
```

Serve the icon files yourself. Browser APIs become available through `globalThis.telocePlugins`:
`forms.createForm`, `i18n.t`, `accessibility.openDialog`, `head.set` and the asynchronous
`pwa` registration result. Use `False` or `{"enabled": False}` to disable a module.
Only enabled assets are emitted. The matching new Teloce version is required.

Forms offer touched/errors/submission state and map server field errors; validation and
CSRF/authentication remain server responsibilities. Subscriptions must be cleaned up.
Translations use named placeholders and Intl plural/number/date formatting.
Accessibility uses native dialogs, focus restoration and navigation announcements.
Head defaults appear in server HTML; `request.compile(meta=...)` overrides them.
SPA navigation uses `head.pages`, or call `head.set` for dynamic pages.

PWA registration is disabled in debug mode. In production, Flaxon serves `/teloce-sw.js`
with the configured allowed scope and injects the manifest link. HTTPS or localhost and
valid icons are needed for browser installation eligibility. The worker caches only generated
JS/CSS plus a generic offline fallback. It does not cache API, Admin or private user responses,
and it does not implement offline editing. PWA registration failures never block mounting.
Listen for `teloce:pwa-update` and `teloce:pwa-error`; activate updates only after the user
has saved their work. Configuration is sent to the browser: never put secrets in plugin options.

The full API and framework-neutral setup are documented in Teloce's
`docs/first-party-plugins.md`. These are optional modules inside `teloce-py`, not separate pip packages.

## Type checking

`python management.py typecheck` checks all registered UI sources through Teloce's optional PyTSCheck adapter. See [the type-checking guide](../guides/typecheck.md) for installation, JSON output, CI exit codes, and current limits.


---

# Source: docs/tutorial-ladder.md

# Tutorial ladder: build a Flask-free Flaxon app in five steps

This ladder teaches the framework in small, verified steps. Each rung has a
**goal**, **code**, a **run** command, a **check** you can execute, and a
**recap**. Every code block here is executed by `tests/docs/test_ai_docs.py`.

## Rung 1 — A JSON endpoint

**Goal.** Serve a JSON response and test it without starting a server.

**Code.**

```python
from flaxon import Flaxon

app = Flaxon("ladder")


@app.get("/ping")
async def ping():
    return {"pong": True}
```

**Run.** `uvicorn app:app` (install `flaxon[standard]`).

**Check.**

```python
from flaxon.testing import TestClient

assert TestClient(app).get("/ping").json() == {"pong": True}
```

**Recap.** A `Flaxon` app is an ASGI app; decorators register routes; typed path
parameters use `<int:id>`.

## Rung 2 — Validate input

**Goal.** Reject invalid input with the documented error shape.

**Code.**

```python
from flaxon.validation import IntField

age = IntField(minimum=0, maximum=120)
age.bind("age")
```

**Check.**

```python
assert age.deserialize("42") == 42
assert age.validate(42) is None
```

**Recap.** Validation errors are HTTP 422 with `error.code == "FX-VAL-001"`
and an `error.fields` map; fields validate with the same rules as the API.

## Rung 3 — Persist a model

**Goal.** Define a model and read it back.

**Code.**

```python
from flaxon.db import Model, fields


class LadderNote(Model):
    text = fields.CharField(max_length=80)

    class Meta:
        app = "ladder"
        table = "ladder_note"
```

**Recap.** `flaxon.db` re-exports Tortoise `Model` and `fields`; connection
setup uses `Tortoise.init`. See [the DB recipe](ai/recipes/database.md).

## Rung 4 — Add admin

**Goal.** Give the model a full admin with one resource class.

**Code.**

```python
from typing import ClassVar

from flaxon.admin.resources import Field, Resource, Text


class LadderNoteResource(Resource):
    model = LadderNote
    fields: ClassVar[list[Field]] = [Text("text", required=True).searchable()]
```

**Recap.** A `Resource` subclass is under 10 lines; legacy `register(...)`
options still work. See [the admin recipe](ai/recipes/admin-resource.md).

## Rung 5 — Compile a Teloce component

**Goal.** Ship an interactive control without Node.

**Code.**

```python
from flaxon.admin import Component

component = Component("badge", "<template><span>{{ text }}</span></template>")
assert component.name == "badge"
```

**Recap.** Flaxon compiles `.vel` components with the bundled Teloce toolchain;
cards and pages render server-side first, then enhance in the browser. See
[the Teloce field recipe](ai/recipes/teloce-field.md).


---

# Source: docs/cookbook.md

# Flaxon cookbook

Four end-to-end patterns, each with code that is executed by
`tests/docs/test_ai_docs.py`. For a step-by-step introduction start with the
[tutorial ladder](tutorial-ladder.md); for canonical minimal examples see
[`docs/ai/recipes/`](ai/recipes/api.md).

## Approve an action

Declare a class-based action with authorisation and a typed result.

```python
from flaxon.admin.actions import Action, ActionContext, ActionResult


class ApproveOrders(Action):
    name = "approve_orders"
    label = "Approve orders"
    permission = "order.manager"
    confirmation = "Approve the selected orders?"

    async def handle(self, context: ActionContext) -> ActionResult:
        return ActionResult.ok("Approved")


assert ApproveOrders().get_name() == "approve_orders"
```

Unauthorised users get 403 with no side effects; failures are reported per
record. See [the action guide](guides/admin-actions.md).

## Import CSV safely

Map columns, enforce caps and neutralise spreadsheet formulas.

```python
from flaxon.admin.importing import csv_safe, enforce_limits, map_columns

rows, errors = map_columns([{"email": "a@example.com"}], {"email": "username"})
assert rows == [{"username": "a@example.com"}]
assert errors == []
assert csv_safe("=SUM(A1)") == "'=SUM(A1)"
enforce_limits(payload_bytes=10, row_count=1, max_bytes=100, max_rows=5)
```

Exports pass every value through `csv_safe`; imports support a dry run and
row-level errors. See [the filters and safety guide](guides/admin-filters-and-safety.md).

## Render a revenue chart

Metrics compute in SQL and render as inline SVG, offline and dark-mode aware.

```python
from flaxon.admin.metrics import Trend

revenue = Trend("Revenue", range="30d", description="Last 30 days")
assert revenue.title == "Revenue"
assert revenue.kind == "trend"
```

See [the metrics guide](guides/admin-metrics.md).

## Add a custom field

A Teloce field is a validated `Field` with a component and an HTML fallback.

```python
from flaxon.admin import Component, TeloceField

sentiment = TeloceField(
    "sentiment",
    Component("sentiment", "<template><select :name='name'></select></template>"),
    fallback="select",
    fallback_choices=[("happy", "Happy"), ("sad", "Sad")],
)
assert sentiment.schema_entry()["kind"] == "teloce"
assert sentiment.clean("happy") == "happy"
```

See [the extensions guide](guides/admin-extensions.md) to package the field as
a `flaxon-admin-*` plugin.
